pageTitle: C1 - interview sizing and the backlog sweep
standfirst: Seven batches, seventeen items. Every step below was run by an agent on this machine and its evidence is committed; you are asked for a VERDICT, not for labour. That is itself one of the things this change shipped. Run the gate first, then read each step and mark it.

gate.intro: Run the gate before recording any verdict. These are plain commands with no backslashes and no invisible characters, so nothing between this page and your clipboard can mangle them; they behave the same in cmd.exe, PowerShell and Git Bash.
checks: The second command must exit 0. That proves the build this page describes, 66732c6, is contained in the tree you are testing. It is a command you run, not two SHAs you compare by eye - on every previous page this gate could never agree, because committing the page moves HEAD past the build it describes.

The third command must print nothing. Empty output IS the verdict: the pathspec excludes the ledger directory, so anything it prints is a real code change made after the build you are testing. You never read a list to reach an answer.
If the second command exits 1, stop: you are not on the tree this page describes. If the third prints paths, stop and tell me what it printed.

sections.title: B01 - wrapped polish items in the fence tool
sections.blurb: The mechanical fence checker could not read this repository's own ~90-character wrap convention, so a wrapped polish: item read as tampering.

steps.do: Run the real fence tool over a batch file carrying a wrapped polish: item and confirm it reports no violation.
steps.pass: The tool exits 0 and prints no batch-content diagnostic. On the un-fixed tool the same input produced 43 of them. Corrected: the batch file said 48, which was a pre-flight measurement of an earlier state of that file; 43 is what the shipped tip actually produces.

pre.note: Exit 0, zero batch-content, on a batch adding four wrapped polish items. Control: the un-fixed tool emitted 43 on the identical input.

steps.do: Grep orchestrate/templates/02-batch.md for a wrapped polish: example and confirm it sits inside the Checklist instruction comment.
steps.pass: The example is present AND lies between the comment's opening and its closing marker, so it never ships live into a scaffolded ledger.

pre.note: Example at 02-batch.md:29-30, strictly inside the comment spanning lines 23-31.

sections.title: B02 - interview sizing and the topic-5 move
sections.blurb: Your request: the interview should ask as many questions as it needs. The cap was never a policy - it was arithmetic in the scaffolder telling it to merge topics down to fit one call.

steps.do: Grep scaffolding.md and SKILL.md for the three retired phrases: the 4-question-cap sentence, the literal pairing set, and the one-consolidated-round promise.
steps.pass: All three are absent from both files. Their absence is what proves the old default is gone rather than buried under a new paragraph. Note these phrases WRAP across lines in the source, so a line-based grep returns zero even when they are present.

pre.note: All three absent, whitespace-collapsed, case-sensitive and insensitive. Control: a phrase known to be present was found by the same instrument.

steps.do: Sweep the repository for every interview #N citation and print the distinct set of N.
steps.pass: The set is exactly {1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7}. No citation of topic 5 survives outside the ledger, which legitimately quotes it as the text being removed.

pre.note: Set outside .agents/ is exactly {1,2,3,4,6,7}. Control: the .agents/-included sweep found five interview #5 citations, so the instrument can see them.

steps.do: Read the interview section of scaffolding.md and procedure step 7.
steps.pass: Back-to-back calls are stated as the default; the compound-label ban carries a real example; step 7 names weights alongside plan, wave map, checkpoints and fold-ins.

pre.note: All three present and imperative at the three entry points a reader may stop at.

sections.title: B03 - leading YAML indicator characters
sections.blurb: A frontmatter value starting with an indicator character is a YAML error, and the end state is severe: the document does not parse, no definition loads, and a read-only role inherits the whole tool catalogue.

steps.do: Run the full suite and confirm the agent-definitions frontmatter cases pass, including the indicator sweep.
steps.pass: All nine indicator characters are rejected at the head of an unquoted value, and the member list carries a size assertion so the sweep cannot silently shrink.

pre.note: 306/306. Nine members swept with size and distinctness assertions present.

steps.do: Confirm the four shipped definitions under .claude/agents/ still parse and still report their exact tool lists.
steps.pass: implementer, reviewer, test-hunter and qa-runner all load; none is rejected by the new rule.

pre.note: All four load with their exact agreed tool lists.

sections.title: B04 - name check-attr in the manual fallback
sections.blurb: The manual fallback stated the resolved-filter rule but, unlike its neighbours, named no command - so a human working it by hand had the rule without the tool.

steps.do: Grep both protocol.md and templates/00-READBEFORE.md for check-attr in the resolved-filter sentence.

pre.note: protocol.md:216 and 00-READBEFORE.md:162 both name git check-attr filter.

steps.do: Confirm the edit reflowed nothing: git diff --check is clean and the paragraph around each edited line is unchanged.
steps.pass: git diff --check is clean and no line in either paragraph other than the edited ones differs from the base. Corrected: the batch file said 'exactly one line per file'. B04 touched TWO lines per file once its review polish landed - the second renames 'such filters' to 'such filter drivers' so a reader cannot bind it to the probe they were just told to run.

pre.note: git diff --check clean; nothing reflowed. The one-line claim was stale, not the edit.

sections.title: B05 - a test seam for the unreachable evidence guards
sections.blurb: Two fail-closed guards could not be reached by any fixture, so flipping either to return true left the suite green while the helper reported clean and then ran git status with a filter driver configured.

steps.do: Confirm the guard paths BL-009 named are exercised, and read the residual below.
steps.pass: The two guards BL-009 named are covered, and so is a third the backlog never named, found during review. Known residual, deliberately deferred: a FOURTH guard in the same function - the path-inventory terminator - has no coverage; disarming it leaves the suite green. I routed it to the backlog during this batch's review because covering it needs a second exported classifier for a different parse, which is new production surface rather than completing the seam this batch built. The pre-smoke runner applied a stricter reading than the step's wording and reported it as a failure; both its finding and my reasoning are recorded in the ledger. Mark this step Fail if you disagree with that scope call.

pre.note: The two named guards plus a third are covered; a fourth is not. See the residual in the Pass text - this is a scope decision, not a defect.

steps.do: Confirm the evidence tool's published surface did not change.
steps.pass: --help is byte-identical to the ledger base and there are still seven published recipes, so no CLI subcommand or flag was added and the mirrored span is untouched.

pre.note: --help byte-identical to base, 557 bytes, same SHA-256. Seven recipes.

sections.title: B06 - build identity, sidecar coherence and hand-over proofing
sections.blurb: The build-identity gate on every previous page had never worked on any run. This page is the fix, dogfooded - it was built by the repaired builder and had to pass its own new rules.

steps.do: Feed the builder a sidecar whose gate carries no containment check.
steps.pass: The builder rejects it and names the missing check. Before this change it built the page happily, which is how the gate came to resolve to eyeballing.

pre.note: Rejected, exit 1, all three missing checks named.

steps.do: Feed the builder a sidecar carrying an invisible control character inside a copyable command, and a second carrying a Section reference that resolves to nothing.
steps.pass: Both are rejected. These are two of the three structurally detectable defects that shipped in the previous checkpoint page.

pre.note: Both rejected, exit 1. The NUL was built with String.fromCharCode, never an escape in a shell-written script.

steps.do: Feed the builder a well-formed sidecar carrying a containment check, tabs and newlines, and only resolving cross-references.
steps.pass: It is accepted and the page builds. This positive control is what proves the three rejections above are not simply rejecting everything.

steps.do: Read the gate at the top of this page, then run its second and third commands.
steps.pass: The gate carries git merge-base --is-ancestor as a command you execute, not prose asking you to compare two SHAs by eye. This page is the fix, dogfooded.

pre.note: Present in both documents. Run here: ancestor exits 0 with empty diff; a non-ancestor exits 1 and the diff names 17 paths.

sections.title: B07 - self-check code spans and honest runner classification
sections.blurb: The scaffolder's own self-check called every placeholder-looking token an unfilled slot, including ones inside code spans - so this very ledger tripped it. And steps were being tagged human on the basis of what test fixtures can do rather than what an agent can.

steps.do: Run the scaffolder self-check over this ledger's own directory as the revised rule states it, discounting hits inside fenced and inline code spans.
steps.pass: Zero hits outside code spans. Raw, the directory produces dozens - every one inside a code span, because naming a placeholder is the only way to describe repointing it.

pre.note: 72 raw hits, 0 outside code spans. Control: a bare token survives the masker while inline, fenced and line-break-wrapped ones are discounted.

steps.do: Sweep all five documents that carry a Runner default and print each one's rule.
steps.pass: All five state that a step is human ONLY when it needs a device, a GUI, held credentials, a look-and-see judgement, or something the environment contract forbids an agent here to do - and each names the live-data and another-OS grounds as that last kind. None still says 'default human' unqualified.

pre.note: Six occurrences across five documents, every ground present in each; zero surviving default-human spellings.

steps.do: Confirm execution-models.md states that a checkpoint asks the user for a verdict, not for labour.
steps.pass: The sentence is present - which is the rule this very checkpoint was built to follow, since all eighteen steps were agent-run and none was handed to you as work.
